name: jetbrains-git-control
description: Bring IntelliJ IDEA / JetBrains Git experience to VS Code & Cursor: Git graph visualization, IDEA-style commit panel with shelf/stash, branch management, cherry-pick, rebase, merge, 3-way merge editor, inline git blame annotations, and context menus. The best JetBrains Git alternative for Visual Studio Code.

colors.description: Color of added files and lines (File Status: Added)
Color of modified files and lines (File Status: Modified)
Color of deleted files and lines (File Status: Deleted)
Color of files not yet tracked by Git (File Status: unversioned)
Color of Git-ignored files (File Status: Ignored)
Color of files with unresolved merge conflicts (File Status: Merged with conflicts)

enumDescriptions: Follow the branch's own `branch.<name>.rebase` or the repository's `pull.rebase` (merge when neither is set).
Always merge the upstream changes into the current branch.
Always rebase the current branch onto its upstream.
jgc.update.method.markdownDescription: How *Update* integrates upstream changes into the current branch.

enumDescriptions: Stash tracked local changes before updating and restore them afterwards.
Shelve tracked local changes before updating and restore them afterwards.
jgc.update.saveChangesPolicy.markdownDescription: Where local changes are parked while an update, rebase or checkout runs, then restored.

jgc.push.autoSetUpstream.markdownDescription: Push a branch that has no upstream with `--set-upstream`, so it tracks the remote branch from then on. Turn this off to push without setting tracking.

enumDescriptions: Ask each time a push is rejected because the remote has new commits.
Merge the remote changes into the current branch, then push again.
Rebase the current branch onto the remote changes, then push again.
jgc.push.rejectedAction.markdownDescription: What to do when a push is rejected because the remote has commits you do not have. Force push with lease is never remembered; it is always an explicit choice.

jgc.protectedBranches.markdownDescription: Branch names that are protected. Force pushing to them (including with lease) is refused, and deleting them asks for explicit confirmation. `*` matches any run of characters, e.g. `release/*`. Matching is case-sensitive and applies to the whole branch name.

jgc.decorations.enabled.markdownDescription: Show Git decorations: file colors in the Explorer and change markers in the line-number gutter. Turn this off to fall back to VS Code's built-in Git decorations alone.

jgc.decorations.fileColors.markdownDescription: Color file names in the Explorer by Git status. Colors are the `jgc.decoration.*` entries under **Color Customizations**.

jgc.commit.signOff.markdownDescription: Add a `Signed-off-by` trailer to every commit made from the Commit panel (`git commit --signoff`).

jgc.commit.runHooks.markdownDescription: Run Git hooks (`pre-commit`, `commit-msg`) when committing from the Commit panel. Turn this off to commit with `--no-verify`.

enumDescriptions: Follow Git config: sign when `commit.gpgsign` is true.
Always sign commits made from the Commit panel (`git commit --gpg-sign`).
Never sign commits made from the Commit panel (`git commit --no-gpg-sign`).
jgc.commit.gpgSign.markdownDescription: Whether commits made from the Commit panel are signed with GPG. Use the **JGC: Choose GPG Signing Key...** command to pick the key for a repository.

jgc.commit.warnLargeFiles.markdownDescription: Ask for confirmation before committing files larger than `#jgc.commit.largeFileThresholdMB#`.

jgc.commit.largeFileThresholdMB.markdownDescription: Size in megabytes above which a file is reported by `#jgc.commit.warnLargeFiles#`.

jgc.commit.warnCrlf.markdownDescription: Ask for confirmation before committing files whose CRLF line separators would be stored as they are (not converted by `core.autocrlf` or `.gitattributes`).

jgc.commit.warnDetachedHead.markdownDescription: Ask for confirmation before committing while HEAD is detached or a rebase is in progress.

jgc.commit.warnMissingIdentity.markdownDescription: Ask for confirmation before committing when Git `user.name` or `user.email` is not set.

jgc.changelists.enabled.markdownDescription: Group the working-tree changes in the Commit panel and the Changes view into named changelists, like IntelliJ IDEA and Rider. Changelists are stored in the repository's git directory and never touch the index, so the Staged group behaves exactly as it does without them. Turn this off to get a single *Changes* group.

jgc.changelists.offerMoveOnPartialCommit.markdownDescription: After committing only some of the files in a changelist, offer to move the files that were left behind to a new changelist.

jgc.decorations.gutterMarkers.markdownDescription: Draw a colored marker in the line-number gutter for every added, modified or deleted line.

jgc.fetch.prune.markdownDescription: Remove remote-tracking branches that no longer exist on the remote when fetching (`git fetch --prune`).

enumDescriptions: Git's default: fetch only tags that point into the fetched history.
Also delete local tags that no longer exist on the remote (`--prune --prune-tags`). This removes local-only tags too.
Fetch every tag from the remote (`--tags`).
Do not fetch any tags (`--no-tags`).
jgc.fetch.tagsMode.markdownDescription: Which tags a fetch brings along. Applies to **Fetch**, **Fetch All** and auto-fetch.

jgc.fetch.autoFetch.markdownDescription: Fetch all remotes in the background at the interval set by `jgc.fetch.autoFetchIntervalMinutes`. It is skipped while another operation runs or a merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert is in progress, and the views only refresh when something new arrived.

jgc.fetch.autoFetchIntervalMinutes.markdownDescription: Minutes between background fetches when `jgc.fetch.autoFetch` is on.

enumDescriptions: Short commit hash
Author date
Author name
Commit number (1 = newest)

jgc.blame.columns.description: Which columns to show in inline Git blame annotations. Display order is always: Revision → Date → Author → Commit Number.

enumDescriptions: A distinct color per author
JetBrains-style coloring by commit age: recent commits stand out, old ones fade
Hide coloring: fixed foreground colors (#jgc.blame.foregroundColorLight# / #jgc.blame.foregroundColorDark#)
jgc.blame.colorMode.description: How inline Git blame annotations are colored.

enumDescriptions: Author initials (e.g. ZS)
Last name only
First name only
Full name
Author email
jgc.blame.nameStyle.description: How the author name is displayed in inline Git blame annotations.

jgc.blame.dateFormat.description: Date format for inline blame annotations. Tokens: yyyy MM dd HH mm ss.

jgc.blame.foregroundColorLight.description: Inline blame annotation color for light themes.

jgc.blame.foregroundColorDark.description: Inline blame annotation color for dark themes.

jgc.caretBlame.enabled.description: Enable the caret line-end blame: `Who, date * summary` at the end of the line the caret is on. Turn off to hide it and keep the full inline blame annotations.

jgc.caretBlame.format.description: Template for the caret blame text. Tokens: ${who} (author name, or You for your own commits and uncommitted lines), ${date} (formatted by jgc.blame.dateFormat, default yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm), ${message} (commit summary), ${hash} (short hash).

jgc.caretBlame.messageMaxLength.description: Maximum number of characters of the commit summary (${message}); longer summaries end with an ellipsis. Other parts of the template are never truncated.

jgc.blame.ignoreWhitespace.description: Ignore whitespace changes when attributing lines in blame (`git blame -w`), so re-indenting or reformatting does not take over a line's author. Applies to the blame annotations and the caret blame.

enumDescriptions: Do not follow moved or copied lines: a moved line belongs to the commit that moved it
Follow lines moved within the same file back to where they came from (`git blame -M`)
Also follow lines moved or copied from other files changed in the same commit (`git blame -M -C`)
jgc.blame.detectMovements.description: How blame follows moved lines. `outer` is the slowest on large files.

enumDescriptions: Stop, leaving the cherry-pick in progress, and offer to skip it or create an empty commit
Drop the commit and carry on; nothing is committed
Record an empty commit that keeps the original message and author
jgc.cherryPick.emptyStrategy.description: What to do when a cherry-picked commit is empty because its changes are already in the current branch. Every choice is reported in a message.

jgc.cherryPick.appendSourceHash.description: Append `(cherry picked from commit <hash>)` to the message of each cherry-picked commit (`git cherry-pick -x`). Git adds it only to picks that apply without conflicts.

enumDescriptions: Always ask which window to open in
Always open in the current window
Always open in a new window
jgc.worktree.openBehavior.description: Controls how projects are opened from Git worktrees.

jgc.clone.recurseSubmodules.description: Also clone submodules (git clone --recurse-submodules) when using JGC: Clone Repository.

enumDescriptions: Show the dialog offering to disable VS Code's built-in Git extension
Never show the built-in Git dialog
jgc.onboarding.builtinGitPrompt.description: Whether JGC may offer, via one dialog, to disable VS Code's built-in Git extension (git.enabled = false). Answering the dialog sets this to "never"; change it back to "ask" to see the dialog again.

scripts.compile: pnpm run check-types && pnpm run verify && pnpm run lint && node esbuild.js
scripts.package: pnpm run check-types && pnpm run lint && node esbuild.js --production
scripts.vsce:package: pnpm run package && pnpm run build:web && vsce package --no-dependencies
scripts.vsce:publish: pnpm run package && pnpm run build:web && vsce publish --no-dependencies
scripts.pretest: pnpm run compile-tests && pnpm run compile && pnpm run lint
scripts.build: pnpm run compile && pnpm run build:web
scripts.verify:
set -e
echo "=== grep regression checks ==="
# 检查空 import
if grep -rl 'import {} from' src webview/src 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "FAIL: empty import found"
  exit 1
fi
# 检查 <ContextMenu> 是否都传了 onClose
for f in $(grep -rl '<ContextMenu ' src webview/src 2>/dev/null); do
  if grep -q '<ContextMenu[^>]*>' "$f" && ! grep -q 'onClose=' "$f"; then
    echo "FAIL: <ContextMenu> without onClose in $f"
    exit 1
  fi
done
# 检查 useContextMenuDismiss 是否还在父组件里（应该只在 ContextMenu 内部）
for f in $(grep -rl 'useContextMenuDismiss' src webview/src 2>/dev/null); do
  if [[ "$f" != "webview/src/shared/components/ContextMenu.tsx" ]]; then
    # 允许 Toolbar.tsx（自定义下拉）
    if [[ "$f" != "webview/src/commit/components/Toolbar.tsx" ]]; then
      echo "FAIL: useContextMenuDismiss in $f (should only be in ContextMenu.tsx)"
      exit 1
    fi
  fi
done
# console.error must not be the only place a failure lands: the webview
# console is invisible in production builds. Only the bridge module itself
# may log directly (it *is* the error channel).
for f in $(grep -rl 'console\.error' webview/src --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx 2>/dev/null); do
  case "$f" in
    *.test.ts|*.test.tsx) continue ;;
    webview/src/shared/bridge/index.ts) continue ;;
  esac
  echo "FAIL: console.error outside the bridge error channel in $f"
  exit 1
done
echo "PASS: no silent console.error in webview"
echo "PASS: no regression patterns found"
